# monitorable_server_alert_template (Resource)

Assigns an alert template to a server. A server with no assignment follows the organization's default template. Destroying the resource returns the server to the default template; it never deletes the template. If someone resets the assignment in the dashboard, the next plan assigns it again. Declare at most one `monitorable_server_alert_template` per server.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "monitorable_server" "web" {
  name = "web-01"
}

# Look the template up by name instead of hard-coding its id.
data "monitorable_alert_template" "strict" {
  name = "Strict"
}

# Servers with no assignment follow the organization's default template.
# Destroying this resource returns web-01 to that default; the template stays.
resource "monitorable_server_alert_template" "web" {
  server_id   = monitorable_server.web.id
  template_id = data.monitorable_alert_template.strict.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `server_id` (String) The id of the server, a decimal integer. Changing it assigns the template to the other server.
- `template_id` (String) The id of the alert template, a decimal integer. Changing it reassigns the server in place. Use `data "monitorable_alert_template"` to look an id up by name. To return a server to the organization's default template, destroy this resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The server id; a server has at most one assignment.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The id is the server id. A server that follows the default template has no
# assignment, so there is nothing to import.
terraform import monitorable_server_alert_template.web 42
```
